analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, all supplied patches, changelog head and CLI-reference base surroundings. These units change documentation, not executable controls; no independently supported security regression was identified. changelog.d/feature-waitlists.md:4-7 describes account-only joining, new-setup approval, deliberate legacy/local exemptions and continued existing setups. docs/provider/cli-reference.md head:1360-1385 documents the sandbox gate before installation; head:1635-1727 documents catalog-driven display, Bearer requests, HTTPS/loopback-only transport, no redirects, bounded responses/timeouts, terminal sanitization and cluster exemptions. Installer execution, privileged GPU/fan authority, inference encryption, cache isolation and attestation are not changed by the supplied documentation.
Integration must examine FeatureWaitlistClient/FeatureWaitlistAccess for token-to-coordinator origin binding (A-008), actual redirect/size/timeout enforcement and safe feature-path construction; FeatureWaitlistView for terminal/JSON sanitization; and SandboxSetupFlow.requireApproval plus Cluster.Setup.requireNewPairApproval for ordering and preservation of existing setups (A-018, TB-013, T-061). The documented 404 fallback, unreadable-pairing exemption and local-to-network transitions mean this CLI gate must not be mistaken for authoritative serving authorization: adversarial providers can bypass local decisions. Verify its intended relationship to platform-owned admission and TB-011/T-052/T-053; no backend enforcement absence is established here. No serving grant, Apple evidence lifetime, billing policy or cache change is demonstrated. Implementation units and the waitlist policy contract remain necessary to resolve these material questions; unrelated unchanged implementations are not required by this local documentation pass.
